material.name: LCWT401
material.defect: Surface sink mark (ヒケ) at top fill point due to shrinkage during solidification

trial1.name: Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap
trial1.description: Heat-retention cap applied near top surface only. Air cooling at room temperature.

observations.40min: Top solidified; slight central sinking (bulk still warm)
observations.next_day: Depression on top surface from volume shrinkage (ヒケ observed)

trial1.result: Slight ヒケ observed — better than no cap but not perfect

trial2.name: Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat
trial2.description: Room-temperature cooling. 3 × hot-air reheat pulses (1 min each, 90°C) on top surface only.

observations.10min: Partial solidification; initial central indentation forming
observations.next_day: No internal voids. Depression on top surface (volume shrinkage). ヒケ still present.

trial2.result: ヒケ still present despite 3× reheat. Surface healed but re-solidified with indent.
trial2.key_insight: Short (1 min) pulses at 90°C partially re-melt surface but indent re-forms during final solidification. Longer dwell or higher temperature needed.

production.name: Production Line (Back-fill)
production.description: Actual CBIC production with back-filling and cold air + 5× hot-air pulses (20 sec each).
production.result: Acceptable product within 24.5 min. Minor ヒケ at top surface.
production.key_insight: 5 × 20 sec pulses at 100°C during mushy zone traversal (not after). Cold air (16°C) starts at t≈21.3 min for final solidification. Total 24.5 min — well within 30-min target.

physics_rules.rule: Reheat must reach mushy zone (62–72°C) to be effective
physics_rules.evidence: Trial 2: surface re-melts at 90°C → heals but re-forms ヒケ. Trial 1: slow cap cool avoids rapid quench.
physics_rules.action: Use T_reheat ≥ 75°C for entry into mushy, ≥ 80°C for reliable healing.

physics_rules.rule: Total process time must be ≤ 30 min
physics_rules.evidence: Client target. Production line achieves 24.5 min.
physics_rules.action: Multi-zone step cooling reduces total time vs single RT cool (which takes 30+ min alone).

physics_rules.rule: Biot number ≤ 0.5 ensures uniform radial cooling
physics_rules.evidence: High Bi (> 0.5) causes large T_surface - T_core gradient → higher ヒケ risk.
physics_rules.action: Keep h_cool ≤ 8 W/m²K for R=1.25 cm (Bi = h×R/k = 8×0.0125/0.25 = 0.4).

physics_rules.rule: Mushy zone traversal speed is critical
physics_rules.evidence: Production line spends ~10 min in mushy zone (62–72°C). Rapid quench increases DI.
physics_rules.action: Design zones to slow the transition through 62–72°C. Target T_core ≈ T_surface in mushy.

physics_rules.rule: Short reheat pulses (< 1 min) are ineffective for healing
physics_rules.evidence: Production uses 20 sec × 5 pulses. Trial 2 uses 1 min × 3 pulses — still ヒケ.
physics_rules.action: Either: (a) many short pulses during mushy traverse, OR (b) longer sustained reheat (≥ 10 min at ≥ 80°C).

physics_rules.rule: Cold air (16°C) should start only after bulk reaches below solidus (< 62°C)
physics_rules.evidence: Production: cold air at t=21.3 min when T_bulk ≈ 55°C (below solidus).
physics_rules.action: Premature cold air application increases DI significantly.
